title: Perf bench scratch - latency + throughput notes
summary: Quick scratchpad for 1) microbenching KV cache hit impact on tail latency and throughput, and 2) batching behavior with variable sequence lengths on gpt-7b-quantized on A100-80GB.
content:
Goal:
- Quick experiments to measure latency P50/P95/P99 and tokens/sec under various KV cache hit rates and batching strategies. Need actionable guidance for autoscale config and default batching policy.

Setup (short):
- Model: gpt-7b-quantized (int4-ish profile we use in staging)
- Runtime build: serving-runtime:v2.11.3 (kernel selection: autodetect)
- Hardware: single A100-80GB (dedicated test instance), CUDA 12.1, cuDNN latest
- Client: perf-runner v0.9 (async), 64 client connections, 200 concurrent requests for some runs
- Workloads:
  * short: seq_len=64 prompt (~16 tokens generation)
  * medium: seq_len=512 (200 generated tokens)
  * long: seq_len=2048 (500 generated tokens)
- Batching: slot-based batching (max_batch_size=32) vs dynamic batching (max_batch_size=128)
- KV cache: warm-up scripts to pre-seed cache to reach target hit rates (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 95%)
- Measurement: 5m steady-state after 30s warmup, record per-request P50/P95/P99 and tokens/sec (mean).

Raw notes / observations (first-pass):
- Baseline (no cache, dynamic batching 128):
  * short: P50 ~18ms, P95 ~45ms, P99 ~92ms, tokens/sec ~12k
  * medium: P50 ~120ms, P95 ~230ms, P99 ~540ms, tokens/sec ~3.2k
  * long: P50 ~620ms, P95 ~980ms, P99 ~1.8s, tokens/sec ~700
  -> dynamic batching helps throughput but increases tail latency for short requests (queueing).

- Effect of KV cache (short workload, dynamic batching):
  * cache 75%: P50 ~9ms, P95 ~22ms, P99 ~48ms, tokens/sec ~18k
  * cache 95%: P50 ~6ms, P95 ~12ms, P99 ~20ms, tokens/sec ~23k
  -> very strong wins on both latency and throughput; tail improves more than median.

- Slot-based batching (max_batch=32) vs dynamic(128) at mixed workload (50% short, 50% medium):
  * slot-32: better P95 for short requests (P95 ~60ms) and moderate tokens/sec (~9.5k)
  * dynamic-128: P95 for short requests spikes (~140ms) but tokens/sec higher (~13.5k)
  -> tradeoff: if product SLOs prioritize short-request latency, prefer smaller max_batch or per-route batch caps.

- Long sequences + high batch sizes cause memory pressure spikes (noticed occasional OOM warnings in logs at batch=128, long workload). Suggest: limit batch size for routes with expected seq_len>1024.

- Quantization effects: current int4 profile reduces tokens/sec by ~12% vs fp16 on same hw for medium/long (but latency per request slightly lower for small batches because of smaller memory footprint). Need systematic A/B to confirm.

Quick hypotheses / next steps:
- Hypothesis 1: KV cache >75% gives diminishing returns on throughput but continues to reduce tail latency; recommend default cache warmup policy for conversational routes.
- Hypothesis 2: Per-route batch caps (e.g., short-text routes max_batch=16) will keep P95 reasonable without sacrificing too much throughput globally.
- Hypothesis 3: For long sequence routes, enforce batch cap <=32 on A100; autoscaler should consider per-route memory profile for scaling decisions.

Immediate actionable items:
- Run controlled A/B: same tests with fp16 and quant-int4 with same batching to quantify 95/99 differences (Ethan to run overnight).
- Add per-route default config: short-text (max_batch 16, max_latency_slo 200ms), conv (max_batch 64, prefer caching).
- Instrument: add token-efficiency / cost-per-token logging per request path to console dashboard (Noah to draft metrics).

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- How do these numbers scale when we have 3x concurrent A100 instances behind routing? Does dynamic batching centrally improve or worsen global tail if requests are routed across hosts?
- Need a small regression harness: sample prompt set + golden outputs to ensure quantization/regression not harming quality when we push batch/kv-tuning.
- Verify if kernel selection is using fused attention idx when seq_len<128; earlier builds had a bug that forced fallback which increased P50 for short requests.

Scratch logs (timestamps):
- 2026-03-04T09:12 - ran short workload baseline, 64 clients, dynamic-128
- 2026-03-04T09:45 - seeded KV cache script, targeted 75% hit, re-ran short workload
- 2026-03-04T10:30 - mixed workload run, slot-32 vs dynamic-128 comparison
- 2026-03-04T11:15 - long sequence runs, observed memory pressure at dynamic-128

Notes to myself: keep this doc lightweight. Move cleaned results + graphs into confluence page PerfBench-KVCache-Report once we have fp16 vs quant numbers. Save perf artifacts: /tmp/perf-2026-03-04/*.csv

Contact if needed: Ethan (run A/B), Noah (metrics + dashboard), Samira (quant profiling), infra-sre if OOM persists.

End of scratch.
